title: Harden SSH on the server
instructions:
## Stop the password guessing

`/var/log/auth.log` shows thousands of failed password logins for root from the internet. You are **ama**, an administrator with sudo. Move the server to key-based logins only.

## Do this

1. Look at the attack: `sudo grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log | wc -l`.
2. Generate yourself an **ed25519** key pair with `ssh-keygen` (keep the default file name).
3. Authorise your public key on this server: append `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Make sure `~/.ssh` is mode **700** and `authorized_keys` is mode **600**, or sshd will ignore it.
4. Edit `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (with sudo) so that `PasswordAuthentication no` and `PermitRootLogin no`. Change the existing lines; do not leave the old ones in force.
5. Restart `sshd` and confirm it is still active before you close your session.

files./etc/ssh/sshd_config:
# sshd_config
Port 22
PermitRootLogin yes
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication yes
AuthorizedKeysFile .ssh/authorized_keys
X11Forwarding no

hints: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 writes ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (private, keep secret) and ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (public).
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys appends the key; then chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and chmod 700 ~/.ssh.
sudo sed -i "s/^PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/; s/^PermitRootLogin yes/PermitRootLogin no/" /etc/ssh/sshd_config changes both lines without an editor.
sudo systemctl restart sshd, then systemctl is-active sshd.

checks.message: sshd_config must have PasswordAuthentication no, and no line still saying yes.

realityNote: Always keep one session open while you restart sshd, and test a new login from a second terminal before you log out: a typo here locks you out of a remote server. Fail2ban and moving sshd off port 22 reduce the noise further, but keys are the real fix.
